clue.text: Surprising Romeo with astronauts' antechamber

indicators.note: something surprising is out of the expected order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A startling scene: Romeo turns up alongside astronauts in the room before launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprising' rearranges the nine letters of ROMEO WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean, sealed chamber where astronauts suit up before boarding is called by this name.

clue.text: With housework, a joyous shout

parts.note: split into house, abbreviated HO, and work, OP for opus

explanation.surface: Someone cheers loudly while doing the household chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housework' looks like chores, but is two abbreviations side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of delight or excitement, such as a cheer, is this word.

clue.text: Perfect ravioli and sauce ultimately a luxury starter

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the words ravioli, and, sauce, a
a starter comes at the beginning, so the opening letter of luxury is taken

explanation.surface: A food lover praises ravioli with sauce as the perfect first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or exactly as one would wish, a synonym.

clue.text: With English explanation of Roman numeral, church finally saves lives

parts.note: explaining the numeral X gives the statement X IS TEN
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word saves

explanation.surface: A church sermon, explained in English with a note on Roman numerals, ends up saving lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'explanation of Roman numeral' is read literally as X IS TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lives as a plural noun means states of being, synonyms of the answer.

clue.text: Use too much iron on part of suit

parts.note: on and over both mean above or upon
a club is one card of the suit of clubs in a pack

explanation.surface: A warning about pressing clothes: too much hot iron on one part of a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The iron is a golf club, not a household appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, choosing a club that sends the ball too far, such as too strong an iron, is this verb.

clue.text: Dynamo works for just 24 hours

indicators.note: works as a verb means operates on, so the letters of Dynamo are reworked

explanation.surface: A dynamo that runs for only a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday such as this one is a single day lasting exactly a day's worth of hours.

clue.text: Chopped up and down and frozen

explanation.surface: Food chopped, moved about and then put in the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' looks like a phrase, but 'up' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut into small cubes is what cooks mean by chopping food this way.

clue.text: Order in French from the top of St Paul's?

indicators.note: in means the order sits inside the French word

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A request, in French, coming down from the summit of St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's Cathedral in London is crowned by a famous cupola, an example of this structure.

clue.text: Made a lot of noise and could remain homeless, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
home is IN, and being without it removes those letters from remain

explanation.surface: Someone protests loudly that they may be left with nowhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homeless' takes IN (at home) out of REMAIN, leaving REMA; 'unfortunately' then rearranges COULD plus REMA.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamour is to shout or demand noisily, so making a racket fits.

clue.text: Maybe Shiva's lost city can be found in mostly barren waste

indicators.note: can be found in places the lost city inside the trimmed waste
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a desert is a barren waste
Troy is the ancient city destroyed and lost

explanation.surface: A Hindu god's ruined city might be discovered under desert sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe Shiva's' is 'Maybe Shiva is'; Shiva is the Hindu god of destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief Shiva is the god of destruction, so he is an example of one who wrecks.

clue.text: Old mosquito net I mended a bit

indicators.note: a bit means a portion of the following words, letters carried within them

explanation.surface: An old mosquito net that someone patched up slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' looks like 'slightly', but marks letters sitting inside 'mosquito net I mended'.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time is an adjective meaning former, so it matches old in the sense of previous.

clue.text: Business expert gets mad without small marsupials

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so mad wraps round the expert

parts.note: an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A business graduate goes crazy with no small Australian animals around.
explanation.definitionFit: These banded termite-eating animals of Western Australia are small pouched mammals.

clue.text: May perhaps cut back on computers one is able to keep current

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to keep means the able word holds the current symbol

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A call to trim spending on computers so that one can keep up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is Theresa May, a former British prime minister, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May, a British prime minister, is an example of a person in elected public office.

clue.text: Second person's uniform, covered in gold, given to unknown

indicators.note: given to means the gold-covered part is attached after the unknown
covered in places the uniform letter inside the gold

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An assistant's uniform, trimmed with gold, handed to a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: This possessive belongs to the second person, as 'my' belongs to the first.

clue.text: Buy toaster for upset solver on top form

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Advice to buy a toaster for a solver who is feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like it describes the solver, but it rearranges BUY TOASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase addresses the solver directly, meaning performing at one's peak.

clue.text: Fool spun round getting dose of medicine

indicators.note: round means spun about, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool spinning in circles is given medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured amount of medicine is often given by the spoon, as in the Mary Poppins song.

clue.text: According to Spooner, Marge Simpson gets advanced weaponry

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: Bart's is the possessive of Bart Simpson

explanation.surface: Marge Simpson gets hold of high-tech weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Marge Simpson is 'Bart's mom'; swapping the B and the SM sounds gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guided bomb that steers itself to its target is a piece of modern military weaponry.

clue.text: A lost duet unexpectedly survived

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things not in their expected order

explanation.surface: A duet that went missing turned up again against the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast is to live or last longer than, a synonym of survived.

clue.text: Lie around Malta getting wild

indicators.note: around means the lie wraps about the island's letter

parts.note: M is the international vehicle code for Malta

explanation.surface: Tall tales about Malta getting out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather or a stormy temper is wild and turbulent.

clue.text: Limitless energy source rising American cardinal keeps quiet

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards
keeps means the cardinal holds the quiet

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: An American cardinal of the church is hushed as he rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman but means a counting number, NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the sun is a source of energy that, for practical purposes, never runs out.

clue.text: More affected one possibly raving, being powerless

indicators.note: power is abbreviated P, and powerless means that letter is removed

parts.note: a partier, someone at a party, may well be raving

explanation.surface: Someone pretentious, perhaps ranting, finds they have no power.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means pretentiously artistic, so the comparative means more pretentious.

clue.text: Smaller group sending us over the edge

indicators.note: sending over means turning the word round
over completes the signal to read the letters backwards

explanation.surface: Something driving us to madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the edge' looks like one idiom; 'over' belongs with 'sending us'.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a suborder is a rank below an order, a smaller grouping.

clue.text: Understands king snakes

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A reference to king snakes, sounding like a reptile expert's remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king snakes' looks like one species of serpent; GR is Georgius Rex, King George.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to comprehend it, a synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Objectionable person round in a bit

indicators.note: in means the ring is placed within the small amount

explanation.surface: An unpleasant character described as rather round.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad is a common insult for a loathsome or repellent person.

clue.text: Angry Poles besiege a junction

indicators.note: besiege means surround, so the poles enclose the letter

explanation.surface: Furious Polish soldiers surround a road intersection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland but means sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two roads cross is a junction, by the plain meaning of the words.

clue.text: Counters vehicle reversing in the Great North Road

indicators.note: in places the turned vehicle inside the road's name

parts.note: the A1, read as AI, is the Great North Road from London to Edinburgh

indicators.note: reversing turns the vehicle's letters backwards

explanation.surface: A vehicle backing up on a major British highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great North Road is the A1, Britain's main London-Edinburgh road; its 1 serves as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaci are bead frames used for counting, so they are counters.

clue.text: Material which changed minds, they say

indicators.note: they say means the words are spoken and the result sounds alike

explanation.surface: Some fabric that, people claim, altered opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is a soft napped leather, a type of material.

clue.text: Wingless bird has strong feeling

indicators.note: wings are the outer letters, so wingless strips them from the bird

parts.note: a plover is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A flightless bird has deep emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingless' takes the end letters P and R off PLOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep affection is the strongest of the emotions.

clue.text: Eclipses possibly caught deer

parts.note: in cricket a batsman caught is out, one way of being dismissed

explanation.surface: A news line that deer might have been captured during an eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse someone is to surpass them, a synonym of outdoing.

clue.text: Do over some waiter at El Bulli

indicators.note: some means a part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A waiter at the famous El Bulli restaurant redoing a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: El Bulli was a celebrated restaurant in Spain; only 'Bulli' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat, doing something again.

clue.text: Sign for one fish to go backwards

indicators.note: to go backwards means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A signal for a single fish to swim in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or token, a sign of membership.

clue.text: Pigs take little time for drink with dessert

indicators.note: take means the pigs hold the other letters

explanation.surface: Pigs spending only a short time eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet wine such as a Sauternes is served alongside pudding.
